title: Gate execution vs status-read command semantics are misleading
description:
Friction observed while lead-driving epic 2821e177 (2026-07-03).

The gate command names invert their semantics relative to what a reader expects:

- `jit gate check-all <id>` only READS recorded statuses; it does not evaluate anything. Its output for a never-run gate is "Gate 'cargo-ci' has not been run yet for issue <id>. Use 'jit gate pass' to run it." — yet it exits 0. An orchestrator that runs `check-all` expecting gate evaluation (the natural reading, and what the jit-execution-lead skill's review protocol implies with "Run jit gate check-all") gets a silent no-op: all gates still pending, exit code green.
- `jit gate pass <id> <gate>` EXECUTES the checker. The verb "pass" reads as "force-mark this gate passed" (an override), which is the opposite of what it does, and is alarming to type for an agent bound by gates-are-inviolable rules.

Proposal (naming subject to maintainer taste):
1. Add `jit gate run <id> [<gate>...]` as the execution verb (alias of today's `pass`; `pass` stays as a deprecated alias).
2. Make read-only `check`/`check-all` exit nonzero (or gain a `--strict` flag that does) when any gate on the issue is pending or failed, so scripted orchestration cannot mistake not-yet-run for green.

## Success Criteria
- [hard] REQ-01: an execution-named subcommand (e.g. `gate run`) executes a gate's checker identically to today's `gate pass`, with `pass` retained as an alias; help text states which verbs execute and which only read.
- [hard] REQ-02: `gate check-all` (or its `--strict` mode) exits nonzero when any gate on the issue is pending or failed, covered by CLI tests for the pending, failed, and all-passed cases.
